reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises. E1 only notes oxidative wear as one mechanism among others without showing a protective, load-bearing scale. E2 discusses a protective oxide formed by thermal treatment at 800°C, not friction-induced oxidation during wear. E3 reports friction coefficients for different compositions but does not mention oxide formation or its role. None of the passages provide evidence for a continuous, adherent, self-lubricating oxide scale governing wear reduction.
premises: Friction-induced oxidation forms a continuous, adherent oxide scale on HEA coatings
This oxide scale acts as a load-bearing, self-lubricating surface layer
The oxide scale reduces abrasive and adhesive wear
Oxide formation is promoted by local heating and mechanical stress during sliding
Wear performance is governed by this oxide scale under dry sliding up to ~800°C
